# Mipmapped Smooth Transitions


## Overview
Mipmapped Smooth Transitions applies mipmapping to [style transfer functions](#777-style-transfer-function-1d.md) to ensure temporal coherence and anti-aliasing during interactive volume rendering [S1, unofficial]. It builds on [Mip-Mapping for Style Functions](782-mip-mapping-for-style-functions.md) by smoothing high-frequency variations in style parameters without mixing distinct visual representations at higher resolution levels [S1, unofficial][782-mip-mapping-for-style-functions.md].

## Subtopics

### DVR-MIP Interpolation
A visual representation technique transitioning between [Direct Volume Rendering](#1184-direct-volume-rendering.md) (DVR) and [Maximum Intensity Projection (MIP)](#10702-maximum-intensity-projection-mip.md) to reveal inner details during [interaction](#41-interaction.md) [S2, unofficial]. It uses a parameter $C$ changing from -1 to 1, where -1 corresponds to DVR, 0 to [Maximum Intensity Difference Accumulation](#3571-maximum-intensity-difference-accumulation.md) (MIDA), and 1 to MIP [S2, unofficial]. The style function $S(t)$ is mapped to this domain using $S(t) = \frac{C(t) + 1}{2}$ [S2, unofficial]. This differs from standard DVR/MIP by interpolating between them based on user interaction, allowing dynamic revelation of inner details [S2, unofficial].

## Background
The concept of smooth transitions based on mipmapping for temporal coherence and anti-aliasing was introduced in the context of real-time volume rendering [S1, unofficial]. The specific application to DVR-MIP interpolation was proposed by Bruckner and Gröller [BG09] and further detailed in research on dynamic focus+context for volume rendering [S2, unofficial].
